key_insight: Perceived journal credibility and hype around machine learning may shape whether biomedical and life science professionals accept ML tools, beyond the usual TAM factors of usefulness and ease of use.
clinical_relevance: For healthcare and life-science organizations, adoption of ML may depend as much on trust signals and expectations as on technical performance, which can influence how quickly tools are considered for research and decision support.
method: Cross-sectional quantitative survey of 213 biomedical and life science professionals.
Participants were drawn from EMEA, LATAM, and North America.
Technology Acceptance Model was tested using PLS-SEM and extended with external variables including journal impact factor and hype perception.
evidence_signal: The study uses survey-based PLS-SEM analysis to test an extended acceptance model in a multi-region sample of 213 professionals.
watch_item: Because the study is cross-sectional and survey-based, it can show associations but not prove that journal impact factor or hype directly cause ML adoption.
paper_title: Technology acceptance of machine learning in life sciences: the role of hype perception and journal impact factor.
